record.paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Banach-space analogues of Hilbert-space lower bounds
record.original_question: In tensor-product numerical integration problems on reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, assume for each coordinate space H_i there is a unit-norm bounded linear functional with nonnegative representer h_i, functions f_i and g_i such that (h_i,f_i,g_i) is orthonormal, and a parameter alpha_i in (0,1] such that alpha_i h_i = sqrt(f_i^2+g_i^2). Under these assumptions the worst-case error satisfies lower bounds of the form e(n,F_d)^2 >= 1 - n prod_{i=1}^d (1+alpha_i^2)^(-1). Do analogous lower bounds hold for comparable integration problems on Banach spaces rather than Hilbert spaces?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2. [42]. For all i <= d, let Hi be a RKHS and let S~i be a bounded linear functional on Hi with unit norm and nonnegative representer hi. ... Then the tensor product problem Sd = S~1 \u2297...\u2297S~d satisfies for all n \u2208 N that e(n,Fd)2 >= 1-n prod_{i=1}^d (1+alpha_i^2)^-1.
Open Problem: The lower bounds of [42] are for Hilbert spaces. Do similar lower bounds exist for Banach spaces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. For each i = 1, ..., d, let F_i be a Banach space of real-valued functions on some domain D_i, continuously embedded so that point evaluations (or appropriate linear functionals) are bounded, and let S_i : F_i → R be a bounded linear functional with unit norm (think of S_i(f) = ∫ f dμ_i as a univariate integration functional). Let F_d be a suitable tensor product Banach space of F_1, ..., F_d, and let S_d = S_1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ S_d be the corresponding tensor-product functional on F_d. For an algorithm A_n that uses at most n linear (or function-value) evaluations to approximate S_d, the worst-case error is

  e(A_n, F_d) = sup { |S_d(f) − A_n(f)| : f ∈ F_d, ‖f‖ ≤ 1 },

and the n-th minimal worst-case error is e(n, F_d) = inf_{A_n} e(A_n, F_d).

Background (Hilbert case). When each F_i = H_i is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, the following is known: if for each i there exists a bounded linear functional on H_i with unit norm whose Riesz representer h_i is nonnegative, together with functions f_i, g_i such that the triple (h_i, f_i, g_i) is orthonormal in H_i, and a parameter α_i ∈ (0, 1] such that

  α_i · h_i = sqrt(f_i^2 + g_i^2),

then for all n ∈ N,

  e(n, F_d)^2 ≥ 1 − n · ∏_{i=1}^d (1 + α_i^2)^{−1}.

Question. Formulate and prove an analogous lower bound for the n-th minimal worst-case error of the tensor-product integration functional S_d on tensor products of Banach spaces F_i (rather than Hilbert spaces). That is, identify a structural condition on each Banach space F_i — playing the role of the orthonormal triple (h_i, f_i, g_i) and parameter α_i ∈ (0, 1] in the Hilbert setting — under which one can establish a lower bound of the form

  e(n, F_d) ≥ φ( n, α_1, ..., α_d )

for an explicit function φ exhibiting the same qualitative dependence on n and on the α_i as in the Hilbert-space inequality above (in particular forcing e(n, F_d) to remain bounded away from 0 unless n is at least of order ∏_{i=1}^d (1 + α_i^2)).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for tensor-product integration lower bounds on Banach spaces returned recent work (notably the 2024 paper "Intractability results for integration in tensor product spaces," arXiv:2404.17163) that develops lower-bound techniques generalizing the decomposable reproducing-kernel method, but these results still rely on a Hilbert-space or RKHS structure or a worst-case function decomposition rather than supplying the precise Banach-space analogue of the (1 + α_i^2)^{-1} product bound. No source was found that resolves the stated Banach-space question, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Intractability results for integration in tensor product spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Under the assumption of the existence of a worst-case function for the univariate problem, two methods for providing good lower bounds on the information complexity are presented... generalization of the method of decomposable reproducing kernels.
status_evidence.claim: Recent lower-bound techniques for tensor-product integration still center on RKHS-type structures, not general Banach spaces.

status_evidence.title: Complexity of Banach Space Valued and Parametric Integration
status_evidence.snippet: Develops algorithms, estimates their error, and proves lower bounds, with the optimal convergence rate in the randomized setting related to the geometry of the underlying Banach space.
status_evidence.claim: Banach-space integration lower bounds depend on Banach geometry and no general analogue of the Hilbert (1+α^2)^{-1} product bound is established.
